name: next.js
readmeHtml:
Next.js

Getting Started

Used by some of the world's largest companies, Next.js enables you to create full-stack web applications by extending the latest React features, and integrating powerful Rust-based JavaScript tooling for the fastest builds.

  • Visit our Learn Next.js course to get started with Next.js.
  • Visit the Next.js Showcase to see more sites built with Next.js.

Documentation

Visit https://nextjs.org/docs to view the full documentation.

Community

The Next.js community can be found on GitHub Discussions where you can ask questions, voice ideas, and share your projects with other people.

To chat with other community members, you can join the Next.js Discord server.

Do note that our Code of Conduct applies to all Next.js community channels. Users are highly encouraged to read and adhere to it to avoid repercussions.

Contributing

Contributions to Next.js are welcome and highly appreciated. However, before you jump right into it, we would like you to review our Contribution Guidelines to make sure you have a smooth experience contributing to Next.js.

Good First Issues:

We have a list of good first issues that contain bugs that have a relatively limited scope. This is a great place for newcomers and beginners alike to get started, gain experience, and get familiar with our contribution process.

Security

If you believe you have found a security vulnerability in Next.js, we encourage you to responsibly disclose this and NOT open a public issue.

To participate in our Open Source Software Bug Bounty program, please visit https://hackerone.com/vercel.

aiSummary.oneLiner: A comprehensive React framework providing hybrid rendering, file-system routing, and built-in performance optimizations.
aiSummary.whatItDoes: Next.js acts as a complete full-stack framework built on top of the React UI library. It abstracts away complex configuration by providing out-of-the-box support for hybrid static and server rendering. Developers utilize a highly intuitive file-system based routing mechanism to construct complex application architectures. The framework automatically optimizes core web vitals by handling image resizing, font loading, and script execution scheduling natively. It integrates tightly with edge computing platforms to deliver dynamic content globally with minimal latency.
keyFeatures: Hybrid rendering: Supports static site generation and server-side rendering simultaneously within the same application.
Automatic optimization: Compresses images, subsets fonts, and defers third-party scripts to improve loading speeds.
File-system routing: Maps the project directory structure directly to application URLs automatically.
API routes: Enables developers to build serverless backend endpoints directly alongside their frontend code.
Edge computing: Deploys middleware and serverless functions to global content delivery networks seamlessly.
